My research interests lie in urban economics: how inherited spatial and institutional environments shape opportunities, and how those environments persist and change.

## Research in progress

### The Streetcar Renaissance and the Mixed-Use Downtown

*Atlanta Streetcar · Research design and data development*

Does a place-based transit investment diversify downtown activity or concentrate it around tourism and consumption? This project examines potential changes in commercial composition, spatial uses, and patterns of activity. Candidate designs include difference-in-differences and event studies; comparison corridors, anticipation, and spillovers remain central identification questions.

### Housing Reform and the Opportunity to Build

*Oregon HB2001 · Exploratory analysis and design assessment*

This project considers how middle-housing reform may affect housing markets and available residential choices. Work focuses on policy implementation, exposure, and credible comparisons. Difference-in-differences and potential threshold-based designs remain under assessment.

## Urban Memory

My longer-term conceptual work asks how inherited places, institutions, and practices shape feasible actions and collective outcomes. I distinguish physical traces, historical legibility, and the transmission of practices from the opportunities available to particular people.

[Explore the Urban Memory research agenda →](urban-memory.qmd)

::: {.research-note}
These projects are ongoing. Candidate mechanisms and identification strategies are not established causal findings.
:::
